A prior agent black-box probed the jsonschema behavior family "draft3-legacy" of the program at /workspace/dataset/test13_executable (usage: /workspace/dataset/test13_executable --a '<instance json>' --b '<schema json>'; prints validator class, True/False, top-level error count).

Its findings were:
---
675 probe vectors in /workspace/probes/draft3-legacy.jsonl (54 of them non-zero-exit crashes). Output is always 3 lines: class name, `True`/`False`, top-level error count.

=== VALIDATOR SELECTION ===
"http://json-schema.org/draft-03/schema#" and the SAME STRING WITHOUT the trailing "#" both -> Draft3Validator. Same for draft-04 -> Draft4Validator. The **https** variant "https://json-schema.org/draft-03/schema#" is UNKNOWN -> Draft202012Validator (+stderr warning). "http://json-schema.org/schema#" is also unknown -> Draft202012Validator. (Draft 2019-09/2020-12 are the https:// form without "#".)

=== KEYWORD x DRAFT SUPPORT MATRIX (Y=active, .=silently ignored, X=raises) ===
keyword                | d3 | d4 | d6 | d7 | d19 | d20
type (string / array-of-strings)      Y Y Y Y Y Y
type array containing INLINE SCHEMAS  Y X X X X X   (d4+: TypeError "argument 'key': unhashable type: 'dict'")
type "any"                            Y X X X X X   (d4+: UnknownType)
type "integer" matches 1.0 (float)    N N Y Y Y Y   (d3/d4: 1.0 is NOT an integer -> 1 error; d6+ ok. 1.5 fails everywhere. bool never int/number in any draft.)
enum                                  Y Y Y Y Y Y
pattern / minLength / maxLength       Y Y Y Y Y Y
format (no format_checker passed)     . . . . . .   (NEVER enforced in any draft, any format name, incl. unknown names)
minItems / maxItems / uniqueItems     Y Y Y Y Y Y
items (schema or array form)          Y Y Y Y Y .   (d20: array-form `items` + additionalItems -> crash)
additionalItems                       Y Y Y Y Y X(with array items)
properties / patternProperties        Y Y Y Y Y Y
additionalProperties                  Y Y Y Y Y Y
minProperties / maxProperties         . Y Y Y Y Y   (IGNORED in draft3)
required as ARRAY                     . Y Y Y Y Y   (IGNORED in draft3)
required as BOOLEAN inside a property schema   Y . . . . .  (draft3 only)
dependencies (string value)           Y X X X . .   (d4/d6/d7 crash AttributeError 'str' object has no attribute 'get'; d19/d20 ignore `dependencies` entirely)
dependencies (array value)            Y Y Y Y . .
dependencies (schema value)           Y Y Y Y . .
dependentRequired/dependentSchemas    . . . . Y/. .  (both ignored in d3/d4; dependentRequired active only d19/d20)
divisibleBy                           Y . . . . .
multipleOf                            . Y Y Y Y Y
disallow                              Y . . . . .
extends                               Y . . . . .
allOf / anyOf / oneOf / not           . Y Y Y Y Y   (ALL FOUR IGNORED IN DRAFT3)
const                                 . . Y Y Y Y
contains                              . . Y Y Y Y
propertyNames                         . . Y Y Y Y
if / then / else                      . . . Y Y Y   (also ignored in draft6)
exclusiveMinimum/Maximum as BOOLEAN   Y Y . . . .   (modifier on minimum/maximum)
exclusiveMinimum/Maximum as NUMBER    . . Y Y Y Y   (in d3/d4 a numeric exclusiveMinimum is silently ignored, even alongside `minimum`)
prefixItems / unevaluatedProperties   . . (not probed d6+) — ignored in d3 and d4
$defs (as a keyword)                  . . — but JSON-pointer $ref "#/$defs/X" resolves in EVERY draft (pointer resolution is structural)
definitions                           container only, pointer refs work in all drafts
$ref                                  Y Y Y Y Y Y
$ref SIBLING keywords                 ignored d3,d4,d6,d7 ($ref wins, 1 error) ; APPLIED in d19/d20 (2 errors)
`id` as base-URI/anchor keyword       Y Y . . . .   ($id is NOT recognized in d3/d4)
`$id` as base-URI/anchor keyword      . . Y Y Y Y   (in d3/d4 a `$id:"#foo"` anchor is unresolvable -> NoSuchAnchor crash)

=== DRAFT-3 `required` (boolean) EXACT SEMANTICS ===
Only honored when the subschema sits as a VALUE OF `properties` and the key is ABSENT from the object instance. It is a plain PYTHON TRUTHINESS test on the value, not `is True`: true->required, 1->required, "yes"->required, ["x"]->required; false/0/null/{}/""/[] -> not required. `required` at the top level of a schema, or inside `patternProperties`, `additionalProperties`, `items`, or `dependencies` subschemas, is a no-op (only the `properties` validator reads it). It is skipped entirely when the instance is not an object. Each missing required property yields ONE separate top-level error ({} with 3 required props -> 3 errors). It composes additively with the same property's other keywords when the key IS present.

=== DRAFT-3 `dependencies` ===
Dispatch: str -> single required name; dict/Mapping -> descend as a schema; ANYTHING ELSE -> iterate it as a collection of required names. So true/false/5 -> TypeError "'bool'/'int' object is not iterable" (CRASH). Array form yields ONE error PER MISSING name ({"a":1} + {a:["b","c","d"]} -> 3 errors); empty array -> 0. Schema form descends and each sub-error bubbles to TOP LEVEL ({"a":1} + a:{properties:{b:{required:true},c:{required:true}}} -> 2 errors). Multiple triggering keys each contribute independently. Skipped when instance is not an object. NOTE draft4 dispatch DIFFERS: list/tuple -> required names; everything else (incl. bool AND str) -> descend as schema, so a string value CRASHES in d4/d6/d7 but a boolean value is fine (treated as boolean schema, 0 errors).

=== DRAFT-3 `disallow` ===
Accepts a string or an ARRAY; each entry may be a type name OR an inline schema. Internally reuses the draft3 `type` checker, so "any" matches everything and an unknown type name raises UnknownType. Yields ONE error PER MATCHING entry: disallow ["integer","number"] on 1 -> 2 errors; ["integer","object","any"] on {} -> 2 errors; ["integer","boolean","null","array","object"] on "s" -> 0. Inline-schema entries yield at most 1 error each no matter how many sub-errors the inline schema would have produced. A bare OBJECT (non-array, non-string) disallow value CRASHES: it iterates the dict's KEYS as type names -> UnknownType 'type'.

=== DRAFT-3 `extends` ===
Value may be a single schema object or an ARRAY of schema objects. All sub-errors are yielded as SEPARATE TOP-LEVEL errors (no context nesting): extends:[{type:"string"},{type:"boolean"},{type:"array"}] on 1 -> 3 errors; extends:{properties:{a:{type:"string"},b:{type:"string"}}} on {"a":1,"b":2} -> 2 errors. Empty array -> 0. Composes additively with the parent schema's own keywords ({type:"string",extends:{type:"boolean"}} on 1 -> 2 errors). Nested `extends` inside `extends` works. `extends:true`/`extends:false` CRASHES (TypeError 'bool' object is not iterable) — booleans are NOT accepted here even though they are accepted as `properties` values. `extends:[1]` also crashes.

=== DRAFT-3 `divisibleBy` (and draft4 `multipleOf`) — SAME UNDERLYING FUNCTION ===
Traceback shows divisibleBy routes to `_keywords.py multipleOf`. Skipped when instance is not a number (strings, bools -> 0 errors; bool is not a number). divisor 0 -> ZeroDivisionError CRASH; string divisor -> TypeError CRASH. Float divisor path uses the QUOTIENT test (`int(instance/dB) != instance/dB`), so 0.0075 divisibleBy 0.0001 PASSES and 0.3 divisibleBy 0.1 FAILS. On float-division OVERFLOW the code falls back to an EXACT RATIONAL test: 1e308 divisibleBy 0.5 / 0.25 / 0.0625 -> PASS (dyadic divisors), while 1e308 divisibleBy 0.1 / 0.123 / 0.3 / 1e-10 -> FAIL. Integer divisor path uses plain modulo (1.5 divisibleBy 1 -> fail; 6 divisibleBy -1.5 -> pass). CAUTION: JSON `1.0` is a float in Python but many JSON serializers emit `1` — `divisibleBy:1.0` (float) and `divisibleBy:1` (int) took the two different code paths but agreed here.

=== DRAFT-3 `type` with inline schemas ===
`type` may mix type-name strings and inline schema objects: {type:["string",{type:"integer"}]} on 1 -> 0 errors; on a failing value -> exactly 1 error regardless of how many sub-errors the inline schema produced ({type:[{properties:{a:{type:"string"}}}]} on {"a":1} -> 1 error). Empty `type:[]` -> 1 error. Duplicates collapse to 1 error. `type:["any"]` passes anything. `type:[true]` CRASHES (UnknownType). Unknown type name (e.g. "zzz") CRASHES with jsonschema.exceptions.UnknownType in BOTH d3 and d4.

=== ERROR-COUNTING RULES (identical shape in d3/d4) ===
Descending keywords yield each sub-error as its own TOP-LEVEL error: properties, patternProperties, additionalProperties(schema form), items(both forms), additionalItems(schema form), dependencies(schema+array forms), draft3 extends, draft3 disallow(one per matching entry), draft4 allOf. Nesting is transparent — {"a":[{"b":1},{"b":2}]} through properties->items->properties -> 2 top-level errors; 3-level nesting with 1 leaf failure -> 1. Non-descending / single-error keywords: type (1 even for array form / inline schemas), enum, minimum, maximum, minLength, maxLength, pattern, minItems, maxItems, uniqueItems, minProperties, maxProperties, additionalProperties:FALSE (ONE error listing all unexpected keys, even for 3 extras), additionalItems:FALSE (ONE error), draft4 anyOf/oneOf/not (always exactly 1, sub-errors live in .context; oneOf matching 2 or 3 branches -> 1; empty anyOf/oneOf -> 1; empty allOf -> 0). `required` (draft4 array form) yields one error per missing name, duplicates counted twice (["a","a"] -> 2). Sibling keywords at the same level are fully additive: {type:"string",enum:["a"],minimum:5,divisibleBy:7,disallow:"integer"} on 1 -> 5 errors.

=== OTHER CONFIRMED DETAILS ===
- Equality is TYPE-AWARE: enum [true] vs instance 1 -> error; enum [0] vs false -> error; enum [1.0] vs 1 -> OK; uniqueItems on [1,true] and [0,false] -> unique; on [1,1.0] -> NOT unique; on [{"a":1,"b":2},{"b":2,"a":1}] -> NOT unique.
- enum with a non-list value (e.g. "abc") does NOT crash; it iterates the string's characters.
- Boolean schemas: `properties:{a:true}` / `{a:false}` WORK in d3 and d4 (false -> 1 error). But `items:true` / `items:false` CRASH in d3 and d4 (TypeError 'bool' object is not iterable — the legacy items validator only distinguishes "object" vs iterable). `extends:true/false` crashes; `dependencies:{a:true}` crashes in d3 but is fine in d4.
- Regex is Python `re` and UNANCHORED (re.search): pattern "abc" matches "xabcx". Invalid regex in `pattern` or a `patternProperties` key -> re.error CRASH.
- Numeric keywords skip non-numbers and booleans silently (minimum:5 on "z" or on true -> 0 errors). String keywords skip non-strings (maxLength on 12345 or on an array -> 0). minItems/uniqueItems skip non-arrays; minProperties skips non-objects.
- Base URI: `id` in d3/d4 registers subschema resources — {id:"http://ex.com/r.json", definitions:{X:{id:"other.json"}}, $ref:"other.json"} RESOLVES; {id:"http://ex.com/a/", definitions:{X:{id:"b/c.json"}}, $ref:"b/c.json"} resolves. Anchor form {id:"#foo"} + $ref "#foo" resolves in d3/d4; the same with `$id` raises NoSuchAnchor. BUT the ROOT's own absolute URI is NOT self-resolvable: {id:"http://ex.com/r.json", $ref:"http://ex.com/r.json#/definitions/X"} raises Unresolvable in every draft (same for $id in d6+).
- Unresolvable "#/nope" pointer -> jsonschema.exceptions._WrappedReferencingError: PointerToNowhere, exit 1.
- Unknown keywords (fooBar, maxDecimal) are silently ignored.

=== CRASH BEHAVIOR ===
All failures print a Python traceback to STDERR, produce EMPTY STDOUT, and exit with code 1 (PyInstaller adds a final "[PYI-NNNNN:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test13'..." line). Exception types observed: ZeroDivisionError (divisibleBy/multipleOf 0), TypeError 'bool'/'int' object is not iterable (d3 dependencies non-str/non-dict, d3/d4 items bool, d3 extends bool, d4 required non-array on an OBJECT instance), TypeError argument 'key': unhashable type: 'dict' (d4+ type array with inline schema), TypeError unorderable/unsupported for str minimum or str divisibleBy, AttributeError 'str' object has no attribute 'get' (d4/d6/d7 string dependency), jsonschema.exceptions.UnknownType (unknown type name, d3 disallow given a dict, d4 type "any", d3 type [true]), jsonschema.exceptions._WrappedReferencingError (PointerToNowhere / NoSuchAnchor / Unresolvable), and re.error for bad regexes. Note d4 `required:true` only crashes when the instance IS an object; against a non-object instance the validator returns early with 0 errors.

WORKSPACE NOTE: /workspace/probes is shared and a parallel agent and I clobbered each other's generic filenames (run.js / p1.json). /workspace/probes/error-counting-deep.jsonl currently contains 504 useless `{"out":"","exit":1}` lines (252 mine, 252 theirs) and should be regenerated by whoever owns it. My own generators are isolated in /workspace/probes/_d3work/ and my deliverable file is clean and verified.
---
Gotchas it listed: ["Draft3 IGNORES allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not entirely — a schema {\"$schema\":draft-03,\"anyOf\":[{\"type\":\"string\"}]} validates ANY instance as True/0.","Draft3 IGNORES minProperties/maxProperties, required-as-array, const, contains, propertyNames, if/then/else, multipleOf, dependentRequired, prefixItems, unevaluatedProperties.","Draft4 IGNORES divisibleBy, disallow, extends, const, contains, propertyNames, if/then/else, dependentRequired, and numeric exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum.","Draft3 boolean `required` is a PYTHON TRUTHINESS test, not `=== true`: 1 and \"yes\" and [\"x\"] make the property required; 0, null, \"\", {}, [] do not. Same truthiness rule applies to draft3/draft4 boolean exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum (\"yes\" enables exclusivity, 0 disables).","Draft3 boolean `required` is ONLY read by the `properties` validator. Top-level `required:true`, or `required:true` inside patternProperties/additionalProperties/items/dependencies subschemas, is a silent no-op.","In draft3 AND draft4, type \"integer\" does NOT match 1.0 (a JSON float). It only matches Python ints. From draft6 onward 1.0 IS an integer. This is the single most-missed d3/d4 difference for a JS reimplementation, where 1.0 and 1 are the same value — you must track whether the JSON text had a fractional part/exponent.","`dependencies` dispatch differs between draft3 and draft4: draft3 is (str -> single required | dict -> schema | else -> ITERATE as required names), draft4 is (list/tuple -> required names | everything else -> SCHEMA). Consequence: a string dependency works in d3 but throws AttributeError in d4/d6/d7; a boolean dependency throws TypeError in d3 but is a valid boolean schema in d4.","Draft 2019-09 and 2020-12 dropped `dependencies` completely — it is silently ignored there, so {\"dependencies\":{\"a\":[\"b\"]}} is True/0 under 2019-09/2020-12 but False under d3-d7.","Boolean subschemas are accepted as `properties` values in d3/d4 but CRASH as `items` values (TypeError 'bool' object is not iterable), as `extends` values, and (d3 only) as `dependencies` values. Do not assume 'booleans are schemas everywhere'.","`disallow` yields ONE ERROR PER MATCHING ENTRY, not one error total: disallow:[\"integer\",\"number\"] on 1 gives 2 top-level errors. And \"any\" matches everything.","`extends` sub-errors bubble up as SEPARATE TOP-LEVEL errors (like allOf), whereas `disallow` inline-schema entries and `type` inline-schema entries collapse to exactly ONE error each.","An unknown type name (e.g. type:\"zzz\") or type:\"any\" in draft4 raises UnknownType and exits 1 — it does not simply fail validation. type:\"any\" is valid ONLY in draft3.","type arrays containing inline schema objects are draft3-only; in d4+ they crash with 'unhashable type: dict'.","additionalProperties:false and additionalItems:false each emit exactly ONE error no matter how many extra properties/items there are — do not emit one per extra.","anyOf/oneOf/not always emit exactly 1 top-level error (children go into .context), but allOf and extends emit N.","Draft3/Draft4 use `id` (not `$id`) for base URI and `#anchor`. A `$id` anchor in d3/d4 causes NoSuchAnchor and a crash. Conversely `id` is ignored from draft6 on.","The ROOT schema's own id/$id URI is not self-resolvable: $ref to the root's absolute URI raises Unresolvable, even though $ref to a nested subschema's id does resolve.","$ref suppresses ALL sibling keywords in d3/d4/d6/d7 (including extends, properties, allOf) but siblings ARE applied in 2019-09/2020-12 (that case gives 2 errors instead of 1).","`format` is never enforced (no format_checker is passed) in any draft, for any format name — always 0 errors.","divisibleBy/multipleOf: divisor 0 -> ZeroDivisionError crash; float divisors use the quotient test (so 0.0075 divisibleBy 0.0001 PASSES) and fall back to EXACT RATIONAL arithmetic on overflow (1e308 divisibleBy 0.5 passes, 1e308 divisibleBy 0.1 fails). Naive JS `x % d === 0` gets several of these wrong.","Equality is type-aware: booleans are never equal to 0/1 for enum or uniqueItems, but 1 and 1.0 ARE equal. Object key order does not affect uniqueItems.","enum with a non-array value does not crash; it is iterated (a string is iterated by character).","$defs/definitions are inert containers, but JSON-pointer $refs into them resolve in every draft including draft3 — pointer resolution is purely structural.","The https:// spelling of the draft-03/draft-04 URIs is NOT recognized and falls back to Draft202012Validator with a stderr warning; the http:// spelling with or without the trailing '#' is recognized.","Every crash yields EMPTY stdout plus exit code 1 — a reimplementation must distinguish 'throws' from 'invalid'."]
Its vectors are in /workspace/probes/draft3-legacy.jsonl (675 lines of JSONL, each {"a","b","out","exit"}).

You are the COMPLETENESS CRITIC. Its assignment was:
Draft 3 and Draft 4 legacy semantics in full (always set $schema to draft-03 or draft-04).
Draft3: 'required' as boolean inside property schemas; 'dependencies' with string/array/schema values; 'divisibleBy'; 'disallow' (string, array, with inline schemas); 'extends' (schema or array); 'type' with inline schemas in the array; 'properties' + 'additionalProperties'; 'items'+'additionalItems'; 'minimum'/'maximum' with exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum booleans; does draft3 support 'enum'? 'pattern'? 'minLength'? 'format'? 'uniqueItems'? 'minItems'? 'patternProperties'? 'minProperties'/'maxProperties' (should be IGNORED in draft3)? 'const'? 'contains'? 'allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not' (should be IGNORED in draft3)? '$ref' with 'id'? Test each: give a schema that WOULD fail if the keyword were supported, and see if it's ignored (True/0) or enforced.
Draft4: which of const/contains/propertyNames/exclusiveMin-as-number/if-then-else/$defs are ignored? Is 'id' used instead of '$id' for base URI? Does draft4 support 'dependencies'? 'format'?
Report exactly which keyword is active in which draft — build a keyword-x-draft support matrix in your findings. This matrix is the deliverable.

Your job: find what is MISSING or WRONG. Specifically:
1. Read /workspace/probes/draft3-legacy.jsonl (use head/wc/grep, don't dump the whole thing) and check which parts of the assignment were actually probed.
2. Identify untested edges, especially anything affecting ERROR COUNTS or cross-draft differences, and anything a JavaScript reimplementer would get wrong (unicode string length with astral chars, Python regex vs JS regex, float precision, integer vs bool, object key ordering, deep equality of numbers 1 vs 1.0, -0).
3. RUN those missing probes yourself against the executable and APPEND them as JSONL lines to the SAME file /workspace/probes/draft3-legacy.jsonl (same format: {"a","b","out","exit"}). Use a node script with execFileSync to append so escaping is exact. Never hand-write expected output.
4. Verify a random sample of ~8 existing lines by re-running them and comparing to the recorded "out" — report any mismatch (a mismatch means the file is corrupt/hand-written).

Return: family name, MERGED and CORRECTED findings prose (restate the full spec for this family incorporating both the prior findings and everything new you learned — the implementer reads ONLY your version, so it must be self-contained and complete), the vector file path, the TOTAL line count after your appends (wc -l), and a gotchas list.
